name: first trimester bleeding overview
title: Bleeding in early pregnancy: ultrasound read against beta-hCG decides whether the pregnancy is in the uterus and viable, sorting it into threatened, open-cervix or missed miscarriage, molar pregnancy, pregnancy of unknown location or ectopic; each column gives presentation, numbered investigations and treatment in order

root.title: Bleeding in early pregnancy: is it IN the uterus, and is it VIABLE?
lines: every one: vitals · complete blood count · group and screen · quantitative beta-hCG (β-hCG) · transvaginal ultrasound
Rh NEGATIVE + bleeding → Rh immunoglobulin · send any tissue passed to pathology
miscarriage = loss < 20 wk · 8–20% of pregnancies · 80% before 12 wk · location confirmed by gestational sac + YOLK SAC

groups.title: Pregnancy IN the uterus: MISCARRIAGE
lines: the CERVIX (open or closed) and the FETAL HEART decide the type

groups.title: NOTHING in the uterus: β-hCG decides
lines: pain + bleeding + positive β-hCG = ECTOPIC until proven otherwise (an IUD too)

head: h
Threatened
cervix CLOSED · heart PRESENT
20–25% of pregnancies
tx: ~• later: preterm birth, IUGR, PPROM, abruption, previa

head: h
Inevitable · incomplete · complete
cervix OPEN
tx: then expectant (91% complete), medical or surgical
• IV broad-spectrum antibiotics + dilation and curettage (D&C)
• 1–2% of incomplete or threatened · sepsis, ARDS, AKI, DIC
• Clostridium sordellii, perfringens, group A strep: toxic shock

head: h
Missed
cervix CLOSED · NO heart
non-viable pregnancy retained
inv: • mean sac diameter ≥ 25 mm, no embryo
• no embryo + heart ≥ 2 wk after a sac WITHOUT yolk sac, or ≥ 11 days after one WITH
• CRL < 7 mm, no heart · sac 16–24 mm, no embryo
• no embryo ≥ 6 wk after LMP · yolk sac > 7 mm

head: h
Molar pregnancy
1/1000 (USA) · 1/500 (Asia)
complete: 46, all PATERNAL (empty egg + 1 sperm that duplicates), NO fetus
partial: 69 (2 paternal + 1 maternal sets), fetus possible
pres: Bleeding · complete: uterus LARGE for dates
• partial: SMALL for dates, few symptoms
tx: complete: 80% cured, 15% invade or persist, 2–3% choriocarcinoma · partial: 5–10% persist
• chorio: no villi, hemorrhagic · after mole 50%, miscarriage 25%, normal pregnancy 25%

head: h
Pregnancy of unknown location
positive β-hCG, nothing seen in or out of the uterus
pres: could still be viable, failing or ectopic
inv: transvaginal: a sac SHOULD be seen above ~1500 (99% by 3150) · transabdominal ~5000–6500
tx: ~• a slow fall can still be an ectopic

head: h
Ectopic pregnancy
2% of pregnancies · TUBE (ampulla 70%) · heterotopic 1 in 30,000, 1% with IVF
leading cause of early pregnancy death
pres: • adnexal mass, cervical motion tenderness, bulging fornix
~• moderate: past STI or PID, smoking, DES, pelvic surgery
inv: 1 · β-hCG above the zone + EMPTY uterus
A normal β-hCG rise does NOT exclude it
tx: • also: same tube before, known tubal disease, cannot follow up
~case: β-hCG 8962, heart in an adnexal mass, hemoperitoneum
• β-hCG must fall 15% from day 4 → 7, else repeat
~• GI, stomatitis, transaminitis, alopecia, pneumonitis, marrow suppression
~case: fell only 14% → ruptured 10 days later → salpingectomy
NO methotrexate if ANY of these → SURGERY instead
• immunodeficiency, liver disease or alcohol, blood dyscrasia, lung disease, peptic ulcer, renal dysfunction

panels.title: Managing a miscarriage: her choice
items: EXPECTANT up to 13+6 weeks: most complete within 2 weeks
MEDICAL up to 12+6: misoprostol 800 mcg vaginally (the one indicated for miscarriage in Canada) · mifepristone first raises success but is approved for abortion only

panels.title: What to tell her
items: about half of miscarriages are chromosomal: trisomy 16 commonest
3 or more losses → work-up + medical genetics
pathology: villi + trophoblast PROVE an intrauterine pregnancy · decidua WITHOUT villi → think ectopic
